name: Chrome zero-day
tile_line: Exploited via web pages. On CISA's exploited list.
tldr: A crafted web page can run code inside Chrome's sandbox, and Google says it's exploited. Every Chromium-based browser needs its fix: update Chrome and relaunch (fixed from 157.0.8103.50), then Edge, Brave, Opera and Electron apps.
summary: The bug is a use-after-free in libxslt, the XSLT library Chromium bundles, fixed on 9 Nov 2026; each of those ships its own copy of Chromium. Extended Stable is fixed from 156.0.8078.96. Upstream libxslt hadn't taken the fix by 24 Nov 2026, and another ID, CVE-2026-125346, was rejected as a duplicate.

affected.label: An unpatched Chromium-based browser
affected.text: Chrome below 157.0.8103.50 on desktop and Android (Extended Stable below 156.0.8078.96; ChromeOS fixed in 156.0.8078.102). Also Edge below 157.0.4341.46 (Extended Stable 156.0.4314.80, Android 157.0.4341.53), Brave below 1.99.56 and Opera below 140.0.6074.17, and Electron apps built before Electron 45.3.0, 44.11.1 or 43.8.8. Chrome only applies updates after a relaunch.

affected.label: Someone visits a malicious page
affected.text: A crafted web page is enough to run code inside the browser's sandbox. Google says an exploit exists in the wild.

do.label: Update Chrome and relaunch
do.text: Open the About page; Chrome checks for an update, then click Relaunch. Any 157.0.8103.50 or later build is fixed, including Chrome 158. Admins: check the version your fleet actually runs, since rollouts take days or weeks.

do.label: Check the version from a shell
do.text: Linux shown. On macOS run `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --version`. On Windows, use the About page or chrome://version.

do.label: Update Edge, Brave and Opera too
do.text: Edge 157.0.4341.46 (9 Nov), Extended Stable 156.0.4314.80 and Android 157.0.4341.53. Brave 1.99.56 (10 Nov, Chromium 157.0.8103.50). Opera 140.0.6074.17 (10 Nov). Later versions are fine.

do.label: Update Electron apps
do.text: Desktop apps built on Electron ship their own Chromium. Electron 45.3.0, 44.11.1 and 43.8.8 (10 Nov) include the fix; their notes don't name the CVE: 45.3.0 moved to a fixed Chromium, and 44.11.1 and 43.8.8 carry the libxslt fix. An app is fixed only once it ships one of these or later, so check with each vendor.
